beats.head: Blackhold Posts First Clean Quarter Under Dabney as Independent Testing Unit Stabilizes
beats.body: Blackhold reported a modest earnings beat, its first since the falsified-records scandal, crediting the newly separated grid-storage testing unit for restoring customer confidence. CEO Halden Dabney said cancellations have slowed and two paused contracts have resumed, though he cautioned the turnaround remains early. Storage shipment volumes recovered to roughly 85% of pre-scandal levels.

beats.head: Brunmark Motors Recalls 240,000 Veyra S Units as Battery Probe Confirms Fire Risk
beats.body: Brunmark Motors has issued a recall covering roughly 240,000 redesigned Veyra S vehicles after regulators confirmed a thermal fault in the battery pack that can ignite under sustained fast-charging. CEO Halvard Renn pledged free pack replacements and set aside $480 million to cover the campaign, reversing much of the momentum that drove recent beats. The newly expanded battery line will be diverted to produce corrected packs, delaying deliveries into next year.

beats.head: Cranegrove Secures Corridor Framework Contract Worth $1.2B Through 2029
beats.body: Cranegrove has signed a multi-year earthmoving framework agreement with the Corridor Infrastructure Authority valued at $1.2 billion, locking in fleet deployment through 2029. Chief Executive Vale Calder called the deal the natural extension of the depot buildout, noting both regional depots will run at full utilization to meet the commitment. The agreement guarantees minimum monthly volumes, giving Cranegrove rare visibility on a backlog that had already stretched into 2028.

beats.head: Halhold Systems Ousts CEO Corin Vale as Board Moves to Contain $900M Fallout
beats.body: The Halhold Systems board has removed Chief Executive Corin Vale following the concealment findings, naming compliance veteran Ilse Marren as interim CEO with a mandate to settle the outstanding litigation. Marren said her first priority is reaching a resolution with the aggrieved partner and restoring disclosure controls across the compute division. The company also disclosed it will restate two prior quarters to reflect withheld outage costs.

beats.head: Korrwright Works Acquires Heritage Movement Maker Alvence in $340M Deal
beats.body: Korrwright Works has agreed to buy movement specialist Alvence for $340 million, extending CEO Dunmore Carrow's acquisitive streak on the back of the Meridienne salon's revival. The purchase secures in-house mechanical calibers that had previously been sourced externally, echoing rivals' move toward vertical integration. Carrow said Alvence's workshops will supply the reopened Meridienne line first.

beats.head: Marlgear Supply Faces Verrant Rail Safety Review After 14-Hour Kessel Outage
beats.body: Verrant Rail's oversight board has opened a formal reliability review of the Kessel platform following the 14-hour operational halt, demanding proof of failover safeguards before expansion continues. CEO Adele Ferran struck a defiant tone, insisting the fault was a single configuration error already patched, while acknowledging penalty clauses could cost up to $60 million. The Halden Mining rollout will proceed but under heightened monitoring.

beats.head: Thronehaus & Co. Beats as Ferrault Buyout Lifts Margins on Award-Winning Marchwick Line
beats.body: Thronehaus & Co. topped estimates as the $610M Ferrault acquisition brought casework in-house, widening margins on the acclaimed Verrand Marchwick line. CEO Cora Dray said vertical integration cut per-unit costs by 18% while insulating output from supplier delays. Salon demand following the Grand Horology honors pushed the flagship line to a months-long waiting list.

beats.head: Venline & Sons Extends Streak With Steady Beat as Second Marden Cleanroom Breaks Ground
beats.body: Venline & Sons logged another modest earnings beat as consumables orders held firm and construction began on its second Marden cleanroom. CEO Mara Garr reiterated the long-horizon approach, noting the new line will not contribute output until late next year. Backlog now covers roughly six months of demand at current capacity.

beats.head: Castlestone Lands $4.5B Multi-Year Grid-Core Deal, Karsh's Boldest Bet Pays Off
beats.body: Castlestone signed a $4.5 billion multi-year supply agreement for its redesigned grid cores, its largest contract ever and a decisive validation of Pell Karsh's thermal overhaul. The pact expands the anchor buyer relationship into a second product tier and locks in demand through 2029. Karsh called it 'the deal that turns a comeback into a franchise.'

beats.head: Garrware Beats as Marrow Valley Fourth Line Comes Online Ahead of Schedule
beats.body: Garrware's fourth Marrow Valley sorting line entered service two weeks early, lifting quarterly margins to 18.4 percent and beating estimates. Orla Holt said the depot now handles a record daily throughput and confirmed the company is scouting a second regional hub as anchor volumes continue to outpace capacity.

beats.head: Lhaus Industries Faces Regulatory Probe After Grid-Storage Overheating Reports
beats.body: Regulators opened a formal safety review into Lhaus Industries' grid-storage units following three reported thermal incidents at customer sites tied to its $2.8 billion pact. The probe casts a shadow over Cole Brandt's aggressive storage pivot, with the second $3.4 billion megadeal now under contractual review. Brandt said the company is 'cooperating fully' and has paused shipments from the new dedicated plant pending inspection.

beats.head: Maison & Vale Beats as Northram Integration Delivers Early Savings
beats.body: Maison & Vale reported quarterly operating income of $1.9 billion, ahead of the $1.7 billion consensus, crediting $180 million in realized synergies from the folded-in Northram cleaning arm. Rhys Kessler said the integration is 'ahead of schedule' toward the $400 million savings target and hinted at further consolidation across the Jansan portfolio.

beats.head: Woldmark's Halcyon 4 Sells Out at Launch as Frayne Declares Turnaround 'Done'
beats.body: Woldmark's Halcyon 4 compute line drew orders exceeding 1.2 million units in its first 72 hours, clearing initial inventory across all regions. Isolde Frayne, appearing at the Meridian launch event, called the debut 'vindication' and pledged to double production capacity by year-end. The result reverses the reputational damage from the Halcyon 3 recall that toppled her predecessor.

beats.head: Wrenspire Pushes Everyroom Into Farm Inputs With Grower Supply Tie-Up
beats.body: Wrenspire extended its Everyroom bundling model into farm inputs, launching a grower supply program that ties seed, feed, and household lines into a single account. Theo Aldous said early pilots across 400 regional operators lifted repeat orders by 14 percent, describing the move as 'the same disciplined thread pulled through a new segment.'

beats.head: Brunstone & Sons Reeling as Internal Memos Show Vault Cell Guard Pro Overheating Was Flagged Before Launch
beats.body: Documents surfaced in the consolidated litigation reveal engineers warned of thermal runaway risk eighteen months before the Vault Cell Guard Pro shipped, with a memo signed off near CEO Halden Crowe's office urging schedule adherence. Crowe, known for aggressive product timelines, now faces calls from three board members for an independent review. The disclosures widen legal exposure well beyond the initial $1.3 billion in consolidated claims.

beats.head: Fenncyon Named Lead Contractor on $3.4B Eastfield Grand Loop Megaproject
beats.body: Fenncyon has secured the anchor role in the Eastfield Grand Loop, a $3.4 billion earthmoving and civil program that dwarfs its previous Southern Loop award. CEO Nadia Ashby said the multi-year mandate lifts total backlog past $6 billion and will require the largest fleet expansion in company history. The win cements Fenncyon as the region's dominant earthmoving house.

beats.head: Blackton Industries Recalls 1.8M Halvern-Line Components as Safety Probe Confirms Defect
beats.body: The safety review concluded that a bracket in the Halvern line can fatigue under load, triggering a 1.8 million-unit recall estimated to cost $310M. Cassian Rode halted the line and pledged to retrofit affected parts at no charge, though two supply contracts have already invoked penalty clauses. The recall wipes out the gains booked when Halvern reached full rate last quarter.

beats.head: Gromford Works Ousts Verrint as Board Installs Caretaker Chief Amid Meridian Fallout
beats.body: The board removed Dahlia Verrint after regulators extended the asset freeze and her personal subpoena widened the criminal exposure. Veteran restructuring specialist Corwin Halstead steps in with a mandate to negotiate a settlement and preserve the group's remaining timepiece lines. Sources say frozen assets and a suspended supplier network have left Gromford weeks from a liquidity crunch.

beats.head: Kessel Drive Hit With Sweeping Shareholder Suit Over Storage Failures
beats.body: A consolidated shareholder action filed in the Merrin district court accuses Kessel Drive of concealing known defects in its storage units months before the recall, seeking damages tied to the stock's collapse. The complaint names CEO Neave Corliss and several directors; the company said the claims are 'without merit' and vowed to defend vigorously as the parallel regulatory probe continues.

beats.head: Aperture Compute to Scrap Dawnmere III Line Entirely in Sweeping Reset Under Venn
beats.body: Marisol Venn announced the permanent discontinuation of the Dawnmere III platform after the indefinite ban, writing down $610M and cutting roughly 1,400 roles tied to the program. Venn said the company would redirect resources to a clean-sheet successor and rebuild regulator trust through a new external compliance board. It marks the deepest restructuring in Aperture's history.

beats.head: Carrowforge Ousts Marlow Demore as Board Seeks Clean Break From Roe-Era Scandal
beats.body: Directors voted 9-2 to remove Marlow Demore after federal investigators tied the falsified test records to units still in active service, naming turnaround specialist Petra Vance as chief executive. Vance pledged an independent audit of every machine line and set aside $340M for potential recalls and settlements. Shares had shed nearly a third of their value since the probe widened.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Signs $3.4B Multi-Site Compute Pact as Reservoir Buildout Scales
beats.body: Sable Renwick unveiled a decade-long agreement with a consortium of industrial buyers worth $3.4B, nearly doubling committed capacity tied to the reservoir-compute program. The deal secures baseload demand for two new sites and includes performance guarantees on uptime and delivered power. Renwick called it the largest single contract in the company's history.

beats.head: Halhold Systems Hit With $900M Suit as Partner Alleges Concealed Outage Risk
beats.body: The partner behind the $900M supply pact filed suit accusing Corin Vale's team of knowingly withholding outage warnings before signing, seeking full damages plus punitive relief. Court filings cite internal reviews the probe unearthed showing engineers flagged the hardware fault weeks before disclosure. Vale called the claims 'without merit' but the board has retained outside counsel and paused shareholder guidance.

beats.head: Lhaus Industries Seals Second Grid-Storage Megadeal Worth $3.4B, Cementing Storage Pivot
beats.body: Lhaus stunned the sector by landing a $3.4B, seven-year grid-storage supply agreement with a consortium of utilities, its largest contract ever and second major storage win in under a year. CEO Cole Brandt said the deal validates the pivot away from legacy auto parts and pledged to fast-track a second dedicated storage plant. Combined storage backlog now exceeds $6B.
